focus: CUDA/Kernel 全框架持续发力，sglang/vLLM/TensorRT-LLM 本周聚焦 FP8 与 ROCm AITER flash attention extend 内核优化。
Quantization 推进 Mamba2 融合 in_proj GEMM 拆分，按输出切片实现 ColumnParallelLinear，提升细粒度量化能力。
KV-Cache 通过 FlyDSL CUDA extend 内核直读 FP8 paged KV cache，避免逐 token 反序列化，显著降低 ROCm 推理延迟。
MoE 修复了 fused GeGLU activation 中 bias 加在 clamp 之前导致的梯度错误，影响多层混合专家路由稳定性。

key_prs.why: FlyDSL FP8 paged extend attention 直接读取 paged KV cache，对 ROCm AITER 推理延迟有全局性改善，且覆盖 sliding-window 场景。

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash carries a ViT tower that is tiny next to the 286 GB of language weights, but on memory-constrained accelerators that is not the right comparison. 
The tower is replicated on every TP rank, so colocating it costs ~0.82 GB of weights per GPU plus its preprocessing and forward workspace — measured ~1.6 GB per GPU on this deployment. Moving the tower to a dedicated encoder server returns that HBM to the KV pool, lets the ViT be scaled separately from the language model, and keeps vision compute off the MoE prefill path.

items.author: 2arian3
items.summary: Adds grammar enforcement for forced tool choices in the Rust frontend's phi4_mini_json parser, matching Python frontend behavior.
items.body:
## Overview

On the Rust frontend, `tool_choice: "required"` and named tool choices are not enforced with `--tool-call-parser phi4_mini_json`: the request reaches the engine without a grammar, so Phi-4-mini can answer in plain text and the response has no tool call. The Python frontend constrains these requests and returns the call. This PR gives `phi4_mini_json` a grammar for its `functools[...]` call list, built only for tool choices that oblige a call.

## Claims

- With `phi4_mini_json`, `required` and named tool choices now constrain the output to `functools[{"name": ..., "arguments": .

items.author: yeshihai
items.summary: Fixes a double TP all-reduce in MoE layers that scales outputs by tp_size when expert parallelism is combined with prefill context parallelism on the naive AgRs backend.
items.body:
I hit this while running GLM-5.3 W4AFP8 (deepseek_v32) with expert parallelism and prefill context parallelism. On the naive all-gather/reduce-scatter backend, `use_all2all_kernels` is true, which clears `skip_final_all_reduce`. The MoE runner then all-reduces the layer output over TP, and the deepseek_v32 decoder also fuses that all-reduce into the next RMSNorm, so every MoE layer's output ends up scaled by `tp_size` (I measured 4.0x at TP4/PCP2 and 2.0x at TP2/PCP4; TP8/PCP1 is unaffected).

items.body:
## Motivation

Hybrid prefix reuse requires Full KV and a recoverable Linear state at the same cached boundary. In the affected `extra_buffer` tracking path, choosing an interior branch in the final Prefill extend can leave its already-computed aligned prompt tail without a separate checkpoint. Subsequent tail continuations then resume from the earlier branch.

This patch preserves both the branch and aligned prompt-tail checkpoints within one GDN prefill extend. It does not split the extend or add another model forward. The feature is experimental and defaults to disabled.

## Motivation

Fixes #51478.

With MegaGate on and EPLB off, the decoder replay tail captures its row-bucket graphs inside a serving forward, after two eager warm-ups of the same layers on a copy of the same batch. The per-forward row-mask cache from #46071 hands the warm-ups' eager masks to the capture, so the mask build is never recorded in the graph. Every replay then reads a valid-row mask computed for the step that captured the graph. Real rows past that count are routed as padding in the tail layers, and prompts whose tail runs from a graph (≤ 2048 tokens here) drift.

## Motivation

With an explicit `--hicache-size` or `--hicache-ratio`, each HiCache host pool checks its allocation against the host memory free when that pool is built, divided by the number of ranks on the host (`host_memory_budget_plain_hugetlb`). The ranks on a host build their pools at the same time. A rank that reaches its check after its node mates have allocated therefore gets a share that their pools have already shrunk. Whether startup succeeds depends on the order the ranks run in, not on how much memory the host has.

## Description

This PR adds DeCo-Attention to VisualGen as an opt-in quantized-attention recipe of the `CUTEDSL` backend. The QK product of self-attention runs on NVFP4 operands, with the quantization error of the scores compensated inside the same matrix product; the PV product runs in FP8, or in NVFP4 on SM120. ## Overview

Fixes #68579. The Python frontend accepts a Chat Completions request with two tools of the same name, while the Rust frontend rejects it with a 400 (`ResolvedToolContext::new`, `rust/src/chat/src/request.rs`). items.body:
## Summary

On SM80, the packed GDN decode path still uses the default BV=32. With FP32 recurrent state, we observed the largest gains at small batch sizes. This PR picks BV=8 for SM80, FP32 state, and K=V=128, keeping 1 warp and 3 stages. Other architectures, state dtypes, and head dimensions keep the existing dispatch.

This is in the same spirit as the SM90/SM100 tuning in #61355 and #63864. I know #65338 is reworking the shared recurrence, and I'm happy to rebase onto it once it settles.

items.title: [Bugfix][Batch Invariance] Make processed logprobs independent of the rest of the batch
items.author: Mazukiri
items.summary: Fixes processed logprobs depending on co-batched requests by always returning FP32 logits under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT, eliminating BF16/FP32 rounding discrepancies.
items.body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` and `--logprobs-mode processed_logprobs`, a greedy request's logprobs change in the last bits when it shares a batch with a request whose logits need processing (penalties, temperature, min_p, logit bias, structured output). `Sampler.apply_sampling_params` returns the raw BF16 logits when no request in the batch needs processing, and an FP32 copy otherwise, and the logprob kernel rounds the two inputs differently. Under the flag, this PR returns FP32 logits in both cases. Related: #68446 (top logprobs also depended on the batch, through `torch.topk`).

items.author: akhilg-nv
items.summary: On multi-node NVLink systems (GB200 / GB300 NVL72), a GPU can read and write the host DRAM of another tray in its NVLink domain through Extended GPU Memory (EGM): host memory allocated with on a host NUMA node with a fabric handle can be exported and mapped by…
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

On multi-node NVLink systems (GB200 / GB300 NVL72), a GPU can read and write the host DRAM of another tray in its NVLink domain through Extended GPU Memory (EGM): host memory allocated with `cuMemCreate` on a host NUMA node with a fabric handle can be exported and mapped by GPUs on other trays. Mooncake 0.3.14 can back a Store segment with such memory (`enable_egm_store_pool`, classic Transfer Engine, `protocol="nvlink"`). HiCache L3 pages placed in another tray's segment are then copied over NVLink instead of through the NIC.

SGLang cannot turn this on today.

items.author: LingZ315
items.summary: HiCache cache-mode storage hits can be lost at two admission boundaries: 1. A capacity-limited prefetch has no active operation yet, so admission may treat the deferred lookup as a miss and cancel it.
items.body:
## Motivation

HiCache cache-mode storage hits can be lost at two admission boundaries:

1. A capacity-limited prefetch has no active operation yet, so admission may treat the deferred lookup as a miss and cancel it.
2. A completed L3 read inserts pages into L2 without retaining them until admission. A subsequent allocation can make the loaded span unusable before load-back (`cache_admission_shortfall`).

items.author: wangbiao0814
items.summary: Proposes RPLRU, a cache eviction policy that grants higher retention priority to reused KV entries over newly loaded ones to improve hit rates in sparse KV offloading.
items.body:
### Motivation.

This RFC proposes Reuse-Prioritized LRU (RPLRU), a cache eviction policy for sparse key-value (KV) offloading. RPLRU gives entries with observed reuse stronger retention priority than newly loaded entries.

Each valid entry maintains an integer age. A cache hit resets the age to zero. A newly loaded entry starts at a configurable age `P`. At each decoding step, resident entries without a hit increase their age by 1, up to the maximum age. When space is required, the policy uses free slots first, then evicts entries with the largest ages among those absent from the current sele

items.author: lkhun9311
items.summary: Fixes TPOT metric recording zero values for single-token or empty requests, which skewed histogram means in disaggregated prefill/decode deployments.
items.body:
## Overview

`vllm:request_time_per_output_token_seconds` records a TPOT of 0 for every request that generates fewer than two tokens. Those requests have no decode interval, so the zeros pull the histogram's mean and low quantiles down. In disaggregated prefill/decode deployments where prefill requests use `max_tokens=1`, the prefill workers emit only zeros. This PR observes TPOT only for requests that generate more than one token, in both the Python and the Rust frontend.

Follows up on #55276 / #55283, which documented the zero but left the behavior as it was. Downstream report: kubernetes

## Overview

Voxtral realtime sends each audio chunk as a streaming-input update. Today, every chunk waits for the previous sampled token to round-trip through the frontend, then re-enters the waiting queue and is re-sent to the workers with its full token history and feature list. That per-chunk cost grows with the session's length. This PR keeps realtime sessions resident in the running batch: the engine keeps the last sampled token, Voxtral realtime stops feeding tokens back, and the workers receive only the new audio features.

items.author: Priya2698
items.summary: waits passes before every rebalance, including the first one. Each rebalance pauses serving, so large EP deployments set a long interval. [Discussion: <!-- mintlify-fork-preview-approval --> ### Preview approval required This pull request comes from a]
items.body:
## Motivation

`EPLBManager` waits `--eplb-rebalance-num-iterations` passes before every rebalance, including the first one. Each rebalance pauses serving, so large EP deployments set a long interval. That makes the first rebalance wait just as long, and until then the server runs on the initial (by default trivial) expert layout, which hurts tail latency early on.

This PR adds a separate setting for the first rebalance, so it can come early while later rebalances keep the long interval.

It is complementary to #43754 (stop rebalancing after N rebalances) and #45282 (asynchronous rebalance).

items.title: [Perf] DSpark: reuse the accept's target probs for the simulated bonus
items.author: zijiexia
items.summary: Under simulated acceptance with top-k / top-p, rebuilt each bonus row from logits (indexselect, temperature, softmax, top-p / top-k renorm) and drew it with. The accept had just built the same target probabilities and dropped them.
items.body:
## Motivation

Under simulated acceptance (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`) with top-k / top-p, `sample_simulated_bonus` rebuilt each bonus row from logits (index_select, temperature, softmax, top-p / top-k renorm) and drew it with `torch.multinomial`. The accept had just built the same target probabilities and dropped them. The second softmax, top-p renorm and multinomial's input checks add 0.24–0.28 ms of GPU time per decode step on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (GB300, attention DP 4, top_p 0.95), so benchmarks run in this mode report a slower decode than real serving would give.

Real serving is unaffected

items.author: zijiexia
items.summary: turns on flashinfer's deterministic top-p / top-k renorm (integer-histogram AIR top-p, fixed-point radix top-k) whenever, so that ranks sampling the same batch commit the same tokens. Under attention DP with one attention TP rank and no context parallelism, th…
items.body:
## Motivation

`renorm_deterministic()` turns on flashinfer's deterministic top-p / top-k renorm (integer-histogram AIR top-p, fixed-point radix top-k) whenever `tp_size > 1`, so that ranks sampling the same batch commit the same tokens. Under attention DP with one attention TP rank and no context parallelism, that premise does not hold: each DP rank samples only its own requests, and no two ranks share a batch. The deterministic kernels then only cost time.

On MiniMax-M3.1-Flash with DSpark (GB300, attention DP 4, top_p 0.95), the deterministic top-p renorm takes 433 µs per decode step at 8
discussion: @claude review

## Description

This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.

A worktree at a new path therefore gets new keys. ccache's `base_dir` setting fixes this, but each user has to configure it. CI configures it in `jenkins/controlCCache.groovy`.

With transparent huge pages (THP) on, two kernel paths can stop a thread for a long time:

items.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deep_select: Opt-in multi-wave cluster top-k for long-tailed rows
items.author: trevor-m
items.summary: DeepSelect's bf16 top-k sends a batch to a cluster kernel only when the batch fits in one wave of some cluster tier. A larger batch goes to the one-CTA-per-row kernel.
items.body:
[by Claude Code]

## Motivation

DeepSelect's bf16 top-k sends a batch to a cluster kernel only when the batch fits in one wave of some cluster tier. A larger batch goes to the one-CTA-per-row kernel. That kernel runs every row at once, so its time is set by the longest row in the batch.

The DeepSeek-V4.1 decode indexer hits this case. With DSpark (6 verify rows per request) and 40 requests per rank, each index layer runs a top-512 over 240 rows. On a Vera Rubin GPU (SM107, 212 SMs) the widest one-wave tier is the 2-CTA cluster with 106 rows, so all 240 rows go to the one-CTA-per-row kernel.

## Motivation

## Motivation

Fixes #51308.

When a token-id prompt ends inside a UTF-8 character that the output completes, `DetokenizeState.step` slices `read_text` at `len(surr_text)`. items.title: [Model] Mamba2: per-slice in_proj so each slice can use its own quantization
items.author: askliar
items.summary: Splits Mamba2's fused in_proj GEMM into per-slice ColumnParallelLinear modules so each output slice (z, x, B, C, dt) can independently specify its own quantization format.
items.body:
## Summary

Mamba2's `in_proj` packs five output slices (z, x, B, C, dt) into one fused GEMM, so a checkpoint cannot give the slices different quantization formats. Like `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`, a checkpoint can now store the slices as separate tensors. ## Overview

FS job completion broadcasts to idle workers because workers and `wait_idle()`
share one condition. Give drain waiters a separate condition on the same lock
so completing a job does not wake workers when no tasks are available.

items.title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Peer prefix lookup-and-pin (RFC 65967)
items.author: briefgaming
items.summary: Implements NIXL-based peer KV-cache lookup-and-pin, letting an idle engine fetch prefix blocks from a holder engine at zero compute cost on the holder.
items.body:
## Overview

Implements RFC https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65967 (compute-free prefix KV lookup-and-pin for router-driven peer KV reuse), proposed by @briefgaming. The consumer (B) asks the producer (A) over the NIXL side channel to pin the longest cached run of a prefix by block hash. A pins it under a lease and replies with the block ids without computing anything, and B pulls the blocks and computes the rest.

This is the engine counterpart to https://github.com/vllm-project/router/pull/509, which routes a prompt to a less busy engine that fetches the prefix from the engine

## Overview

Closes #68428.

When a request skips the media data of some items and relies on their UUIDs hitting the processor cache, the processor rejects the request at the first item that missed. By then it has already found every missed item, but the error names only the first one. A client that resends that one item then meets the next miss, so it needs one more round trip for each missing item. This PR names all of them in one error.

## Claims

- The cache-miss error for items sent without data now names every such item, by modality and index, in one error.

items.author: Wanli-Jiang
items.summary: The qwen4exp cache manager keeps a QSA index-key plane next to the K/V pool. A page holds one row per token (, 32): the token's raw index key, overwritten at the last token of each group by the group's compressed key.
items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

The qwen4_exp cache manager keeps a QSA index-key plane next to the K/V pool. A page holds one row per token (`tokens_per_block`, 32): the token's raw index key, overwritten at the last token of each `compress_ratio` group by the group's compressed key. Index scoring reads only the compressed keys; a raw key is read once more, to pool its group, and is dead after that.

With `TRTLLM_QSA_INDEX_PLANE_COMPACT=1` a page holds the compressed keys in its first rows and two small sets of raw rows (one per group parity) after them: 14 rows instead of 32 at 32 tok

MFSDP v2 can combine up to four microbatch gradients into one inner reduce-scatter and let autograd accumulate into the retained input buffer.

items.title: [Feature Request]Support FP32 bias gradient accumulation in native fused Linear backward
items.author: zjjott
items.summary: Extend fused Linear backward to accumulate trainable bias gradients in FP32 instead of BF16, reducing split-vs-full gradient relative L2 error from ~2e-3 to ~8e-8.
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When `gradient_accumulation_fusion=True`, native `LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication` can accumulate weight gradients directly into FP32 `main_grad`, but its bias gradient still passes through BF16 before reaching the FP32 DDP buffer.

The relevant code is [`grad_bias = grad_output.sum(dim=0)` in layers.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/dev/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/layers.py#L962). With BF16 `grad_output`, this returns a BF16 result. Subsequent FP32 accumulation cannot recover the lost precision.

items.author: Muchuan-Jin
items.summary: The transient that builds calls. The nanobind binding takes the manager by reference, so the first prefetch of a fresh manager, when no live owns it yet, throws. [Discussion: Token conversion and the call to remain unchanged.]
items.body:
## Description

**Issue.** With `kv_cache_config.disk_prefetch_num_reqs > 0` a worker dies in its event loop with
`Error in event loop: bad_weak_ptr`. The transient `KvCache` that `prefetch_reuse` builds calls
`manager.shared_from_this()`. The nanobind binding takes the manager by reference, so the first
prefetch of a fresh manager, when no live `KvCache` owns it yet, throws `std::bad_weak_ptr`.

**Fix.** Bind `prefetch_reuse` by `std::shared_ptr<kv::KvCacheManager>`, like `create_kv_cache`.
One file, `cpp/tensorrt_llm/nanobind/batch_manager/kvCacheManagerV2.cpp`, +5 / -2.

**Seen on.** Qwen3.

items.title: [None][perf] Gemma4 decode fusions: norm/RoPE, FP8 input quantization, PLE tail and assistant head
items.author: amukkara
items.summary: Kernel times are per call at decode (32-40 tokens). GSM8K is unchanged within noise (paired test). [Discussion: <!-- recentreviewstatusend --> <!-- walkthroughstart --> ### Walkthrough This pull request adds ]
items.body:
## Description
- At small batch with speculative decoding, Gemma4 decode is dominated by many small latency-bound ops between the FP8 GEMMs: norms, RoPE, FP8 casts, the per-layer-embedding tail and the assistant head.
- This PR fuses each such chain into one kernel that writes the next GEMM's input directly (in FP8 where that GEMM takes FP8), and overlaps the remaining launches with PDL.
- The result has fewer launches and memory round trips per layer, with no change to model outputs beyond fp32 reduction order.

## Peformance

- Speedups are measured on RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) for Gemma-4

Fixes #2532.

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

items.summary: The torch backend of (the default fused backend) divides the bf16 logits by the temperature before upcasting to fp32, so log-probs differ from the rollout sampler’s formula (fp32 logits / T) by up to 0.054 at T=0.7, and the returned entropy is bf16. This upcas…
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

The torch backend of `FusedLinearForPPO` (the default fused backend) divides the bf16 logits by the temperature before upcasting to fp32, so log-probs differ from the rollout sampler’s formula (fp32 logits / T) by up to 0.054 at T=0.7, and the returned entropy is bf16. This upcasts first, then divides. No open PR or issue covers this.

items.author: shx815
items.summary: When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards report a mean of.
items.body:
## Summary

When context compaction splits an episode into multiple training rows, `rollout/raw_reward` gives that episode extra weight. For example, four episodes with rewards `[1, 0, 0, 0]` report a mean of `0.25`. Splitting the first and last episodes into two rows each raises the logged mean to `0.3333`, even though the episode rewards are identical.

Compute the mean over episodes before data-parallel partitioning. Each episode contributes equally, including when its segments land on different ranks. In the example above, the logged mean stays at `0.25` after splitting.

items.body:
Add OptimizerConfig.fused_main_grad_copy (--fused-main-grad-copy, default off). With it, _copy_model_grads_to_main_grads groups this rank's BF16/FP16 grad shards into runs of adjacent shards of one grad buffer (normally one per bucket shard) and converts each run with one vectorized Triton kernel (megatron/core/fusions/fused_float_upcast.py) instead of one .float() per parameter. Each main grad is a view of its run's FP32 tensor; the conversion is exact, so the values are bit-identical. FP32 grads and the precision-aware optimizer are unchanged, and the path works under CUDA graph capture.

### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

Custom Megatron model providers still need changes to slime's built-in HF loader/exporter registries before they can load a checkpoint and sync weights to rollout engines. This adds two optional import-path callbacks to keep model-specific tensor mappings outside slime:

- `--custom-hf-weight-loader-path`: maps a Megatron parameter/buffer name to its HF tensor. Checkpoint detection honors the callback; loading retains the shared padding, sharding, shape validation and dtype/device copy.

items.body:
Rank 0 creates the --save-hf directory and copies the non-weight files of --hf-checkpoint into it, then the
shard writers on other nodes open files in it. On NFS a client that looked the path up before rank 0 created it
can keep that negative lookup cached for a while, so a writer on another node fails to find a directory that
already exists on the server.

_SafetensorShardWriter now calls mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) on every rank that writes shards. The call
goes to the server and refreshes the cached entry; where the directory is already visible it does nothing.

The SGLang patch stack adds TokenizerManager.post_process_weights, which always takes the writer side of

calls avoid this: update_weights_from_disk skips the writer lock while paused, and begin_weight_update and

items.title: Compute DSA split gradient norms from DTensor layouts in FullyShardedOptimizer
items.author: Autumn1998
items.summary: With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging.
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

With MFSDP v2, DSA models fail at the first optimizer step. For models with a DSA indexer, the optimizer computes the indexer and non-indexer gradient norms on every step for logging. The base `get_dsa_split_grad_norms` goes through `get_grad_norm_fp32`, which requires all DTensor gradients to share one mesh, but the non-indexer half mixes dense and expert gradients. `FullyShardedOptimizer` now computes both norms the way its `get_grad_norm` already does, from each gradient's own layout.

A DeepSeek-V4 Pro proxy on 64 GB200 with MFSDP v2 now runs past the first step.

### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

items.body:
## Problem and behavior

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. The engine now owns a device-bound NCCLGroup specialization with a single-device barrier and a logical group key shared across masked/shared ordinal layouts. Allocation, executor-thread broadcast, synchronization and destruction use the engine device. Ordinary Ray groups retain their behavior, and duplicate ownership/topology checks remain. Delta transfers reuse this group and device without changing the wire protocol

## Motivation

`Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

items.title: [fsdp] feat: project LM head only for response tokens
items.author: hxw12219
items.summary: Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, (default ). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in FSDP engine option, `response_only_lm_head` (default `false`). RL losses read values only at response tokens, but the engine projects every packed token through the LM head. With the option on, the engine passes the packed rows that predict response tokens to the model as Transformers' `logits_to_keep`, so the eager and fused LM heads project only those rows. The values at response tokens are unchanged.

The saving grows with the prompt's share of each sequence: it is largest for long prompts with short responses and small for short prompts with long

## Problem

With `--sglang-speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and a colocated rollout engine, the first weight sync silently overwrites the DFLASH draft with target weights. After that, the acceptance length is ~1.0 and rollout is slower than with speculative decoding off.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

items.title: fix(rm_hub): accept numeric zero ground truth in grade_answer_verl
items.author: Domin-Focus
items.summary: Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct response scores 0 under. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.
items.body:
## Problem

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

```python
if not ground_truth:
    return False
ground_truth = str(ground_truth)
```

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. Both are falsy, so the guard treats them as a missing label, and every correct `\boxed{0}` response scores 0 under `rm_type=math`. Under GRPO, a group where every sample gets 0 gives no learning signal for that prompt.

items.author: Asthenia0412
items.summary: This coupled every submodule of (e.g.,, ) to the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need synchronous rule-based reward functions. [Discussion: Thanks for the review!]
items.body:
## Background

`vime.rollout.rm_hub.__init__` imported `aiohttp` at module load time. This
coupled every submodule of `rm_hub` (e.g. `math_utils`, `f1`, `gpqa`) to
the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need
synchronous rule-based reward functions.

## Problem

Running reward CPU tests in a lightweight contributor environment fails
during pytest collection, before any test body executes:

items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

## Solution

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.

## Background

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

## Description

### 1. Colocate weight sync fails on every GPU but 0 (ROCm)

On ROCm a HIP IPC handle carries the **exporter's** device ordinal, and `hipIpcOpenMemHandle`
resolves it in the **importer's** enumeration; CUDA honours the importer's current device instead.
In colocate mode the trainer exports and the rollout engine imports, so a trainer rank that sees the
whole node exports at ordinal N while an engine launched with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<one gpu>`
enumerates one device where ordinal N does not exist. The two agree only when N is 0 — hence weight

items.summary: When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task except…
items.body:
## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.title: require --ref-load when KL is enabled instead of crashing with a TypeError
items.author: rootkiller6788
items.summary: Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slimevalidateargs with, because it stat'd args.refload before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.
items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

items.title: fix: preserve equals in extra environment values
items.author: imshunsuke
items.summary: For example: was parsed as: This corrupts padded or otherwise -containing environment values. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged.
items.body:
## Summary

- Preserve `=` characters after the first separator in the space-separated `extra_env_vars` fallback parser.
- Add regression coverage to the always-on CPU test matrix.

## Problem

`_parse_extra_env_vars` split each assignment on every `=` and then kept only the second component. For example:

`TOKEN=abc== END=ok`

was parsed as:

`{"TOKEN": "abc", "END": "ok"}`

This corrupts padded or otherwise `=`-containing environment values.

## Change

Use `split("=", 1)` so only the key/value separator is consumed. JSON input handling and the existing fallback tokenization remain unchanged

## Background

In the agentic rollout path, each agent turn sends a request to SGLang through the SGLang router. When a request is cancelled or hits the client-side read timeout, Slime must explicitly abort the corresponding SGLang request to release its scheduler slot and KV-cache resources.

`sglang_url` points to the SGLang router address, but the router does not expose or forward the `/abort_request` endpoint.

Long full-history prompt rendering blocks the agent adapter's aiohttp event loop. Move the existing `_session_prompt_ids()` call to one adapter-owned worker thread, retaining exact upstream rendering, saved sampled-token prefixes, and safe fallback for changed histories/tool schemas.

The worker bounds submitted running/queued work. items.author: EazyReal
items.summary: OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes, not the matched-temperature objective. Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to …
items.body:
## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

items.body:
This PR adds native vLLM Encoder-Prefill Disaggregation (EPD) to Vime. It uses `worker_type: encoder` and composes with the existing regular and PD rollout paths.

The implementation has two main parts:

1. Compile the user topology and group overrides into vLLM EC configuration during rollout-server orchestration.
2. Prime encoder engines from the rollout layer before the existing multimodal render/generate flow.

Related to #11.
